atoms.1: Poison ivy (Toxicodendron radicans) is a plant.
atoms.2: Poison ivy contains an oil called urushiol.
atoms.3: Urushiol causes an allergic reaction in most people.
atoms.4: The urushiol oil is responsible for the characteristic rash associated with poison ivy exposure.
atoms.5: The urushiol oil is responsible for the blisters associated with poison ivy exposure.
atoms.6: The urushiol oil is responsible for the itching associated with poison ivy exposure.
atoms.7: The urushiol oil is not contagious between people.
atoms.8: The urushiol oil cannot be spread from person to person through direct contact or other means.
atoms.9: Urushiol oil can be transferred to surfaces such as clothing.
atoms.10: Urushiol oil can be transferred to tools.
atoms.11: Urushiol oil can be transferred to pets.
atoms.12: Urushiol oil can cause a reaction when someone comes into contact with contaminated items.
atoms.13: People who have not previously been exposed to urushiol may develop an allergic reaction after exposure.
atoms.14: People who have been previously exposed to urushiol may not react at all.
atoms.15: People who have been previously exposed to urushiol may experience a milder reaction.
atoms.16: The body builds up a tolerance to urushiol oil over time.

snippets.output: Poison ivy (Toxicodendron radicans) is a plant that contains an oil called urushiol, which causes an allergic reaction in most people.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: enumeration of basic properties of poison ivy/urushiol.

snippets.output: The urushiol oil is responsible for the characteristic rash, blisters, and itching associated with poison ivy exposure.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: enumeration of symptoms caused by urushiol.

snippets.output: Urushiol oil is not contagious between people and cannot be spread from person to person through direct contact or other means.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: two restatements of the same claim. Expert-false: urushiol oil itself CAN be transferred person-to-person via skin/clothing contact while the oil remains on the surface. The rash (immune reaction) is not contagious, but the oil is transferable. The blanket statement that urushiol cannot be spread person-to-person is incorrect.

snippets.output: Urushiol oil can be transferred to surfaces such as clothing, tools, or pets, and can cause a reaction when someone comes into contact with those contaminated items.
snippets.notes: Pattern A+B: enumeration of contaminated surfaces with causal chain to reaction.

snippets.output: People who have not previously been exposed to urushiol may develop an allergic reaction after exposure.
snippets.notes: Kept atomic to isolate the true atom from the neighboring expert-false tolerance claims (14-16).

snippets.output: People who have been previously exposed to urushiol may not react at all or may experience a milder reaction, because the body builds up a tolerance to urushiol oil over time.
snippets.notes: Pattern C: conclusion (tolerance) + premises (milder/no reaction). Expert-false: this is medically backwards. Repeat exposure to urushiol typically sensitizes a person, often producing stronger or earlier reactions on subsequent exposures rather than tolerance.
